pr_body:
Closes #4334 

This adds an ipc event related to input devices. Currently the
following changes are supported:
- [x] added: when an input device becomes available
- [x] removed: when an input device is no longer available
- [x] xkb_keymap_changed: (keyboards only) the keymap changed
- [x] xkb_layout_changed: (keyboards only) the effective layout changed
- [x] libinput_config_changed: (libinput devices only) a libinput config option changed
pr_comments: This is ready for review. I kept the `input::xkb_config_changed` event in a separate commit since it includes a major refactor of the libinput config management code.

issue_context.title: Feature request: Allow subscribing to xkb layout changes
issue_context.body:
Version: 1.0

I am trying to write a script that would display the selected keymap, and print a new line every time the layout is changed. In X, I use xkb-switch to accomplish this task, as it has a subscribe option.

I can read it fine according to docs; `swaymsg -t get_inputs | jq '.[] | select(."xkb_active_layout_name") | ."xkb_active_layout_name"` works fine. However, right now this can only be polled in a script, which is not desirable (time delay between change events) An event that can be subscribed to on active keyboard layout change (Something like `swaymsg -t subscribe '["xkb_active_layout_name"]' -w` would be useful.

Or, I currently use `xkb_options "grp:caps_toggle"`; using caps lock to cycle through the keymaps. I cannot bindsym to this key now however. 'bindsym Caps_Lock "swaymsg -t send_tick 'keymap_changed'"' does not send a tick.
comments: Maybe we should have an `input` event, just like we have an `output` event

> Maybe we should have an `input` event

Sounds reasonable to me. What events should we expose? Some ideas:
- `added`
- `removed`
- `xkb_layout_changed`
- `libinput_config_changed`

> just like we have an `output` event

Just as a note, the `output` event is not currently implemented (see #4020).

These cover all the bases for keyboard layout changes, and plugging in/out input devices.

At least I can build my entire toolkit that I have currently on X by subscribing to these events.

review_comments: Hmm, not sure I understand the logic here...

Hmm, nevermind. It's the effective layout that gets reset.

However if the keymap changed the effective layout changes too, even if `effective_layout` is still zero. The effective layout depends on the keymap.

Yes, but if the effective layout is 0 before and after, then either the entire keymap changed or the keymap is identical and there is no change to the effective layout. See #4343 for a follow-up for this
